name: cp
purpose: Copy files or directories from a source to a destination while preserving the original.
explanation: Copies a file to a new path. If the destination file already exists, its content is OVERWRITTEN with the source's content. To copy an entire directory and everything inside it, you must add the '-r' (recursive) flag.

parameters.description: Recursive copy — required to copy a directory and all files/subfolders inside it.

example:
cp kitkat.txt perk.txt
cp -r sourceFolder destinationFolder
expectedOutput: (Creates a copy at the destination while keeping the original intact)
whenToUse: When duplicating files or backing up entire folders.
commonMistakes: Running cp on a folder without -r (fails with an 'Is a directory' error).
Overwriting an existing destination file without realizing cp replaces its content.
